reasons: [alternatives_counterarguments/major] D1 [CL5; criteriaAssessments C5; alternatives (no 'reduce n4.large count now' option); practicalImplications] The draft says that, until requests are lowered, nodes cannot safely be removed and autoscaling 'will remove few nodes'. From that it concludes that right-sizing must come first (CL5, C5 assessment, 'Right-size ... then remove' alternative). The draft's own numbers contradict this. CPU requests are 72% of allocatable, about 115 of 160 vCPU. Memory requests are 68%, about 435 of 640 GiB. CL9 already finds that single-node loss fits inside the 28% request headroom. So the cluster can drop some nodes now, before any right-sizing. At an illustrative 85% request ceiling, CPU needs about 34 nodes and memory about 32. That means about 6 n4.large nodes could go, roughly 6 x 140.16 = ~840 USD/month at list price, subject to N+1, zone and PDB checks. The decision objective names 'cutting node count' as a separate alternative. The draft never assesses a direct node reduction on the current shape, and it gives no cluster-specific estimate, even an illustrative one, for any alternative. It leans instead on a generic vendor figure of 30-50% (E12). The decision-maker is left without the one quantified, low-risk option that could be acted on this month.
D1 major alternatives_counterarguments (direct node reduction omitted), remedy reanalysis
